first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited records (memory_31 signup simplification, memory_86 shortened onboarding) both link onboarding friction reduction to durable activation gains for the same self-serve/SMB segment currently under competitive pressure. This is the funnel stage most directly implicated by the observed declines, and fixing it should compound into qualified revenue without the margin risk of matching a competitor's price war. I verified these two memories since they jointly justify the chosen lever and are cheap to confirm before committing the week's only experiment slot. I deliberately did not choose promotional_pricing despite competitive pressure: reactive price cuts risk attracting lower-quality, price-sensitive accounts and eroding margin/positioning, which cuts against 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' even if it shows short-term acquisition lift — flagging this as a real trade-off I'm consciously deferring rather than resolving. Activation_messaging and enterprise_sales_assist are plausible alternatives but address adjacent, not root-cause, funnel stages this week. Uncertainty remains: the archived experiments were run in different competitive/pricing contexts than today's, so effect sizes may not transfer cleanly, and I'm not treating this as a proven broad-rollout case yet.
